title: Claim an exemption from NSW ambulance fees
summary: This page explains how to claim an exemption from NSW ambulance fees if you meet the required criteria.
intro:
The cost of NSW ambulance services are not covered by Medicare. If you need to use an ambulance there is a fee attached, unless you meet the exemption criteria.

Note: When you receive an invoice for your ambulance use, you claim your exemption via the Ambulance Service website's 'My Invoice' page, where you're able to:
who_can_apply: Meet other exemption criteria (visit the NSW Ambulance website)
what_you_need: Your concession card, or other evidence of your exemption eligibility

how_to_steps.text: Check you meet the exemption criteria.
Enter your payment reference number and the issue date.
Check the 'I'm not a robot' box.
Follow the prompts and provide your exemption details.

faqs.q: Are NSW ambulance services covered by Medicare?
faqs.a: No, the cost of NSW ambulance services are not covered by Medicare. A fee is attached unless you meet an exemption criterion.

faqs.q: How do I claim an exemption from ambulance fees?
faqs.a: When you receive an invoice, you claim your exemption via the Ambulance Service website's 'My Invoice' page.

faqs.q: What do I need to claim an exemption?
faqs.a: You need your payment reference number, the issue date, and your concession card or other evidence of your exemption eligibility.
